phase_0.boundary_condition: The scale-collapse boundary (𐑦) where the fusion interface fully encodes and transfers internal state losslessly, making surface and interior a single register; this boundary is the cyclic figure-8 topology (𐑥) that contains the hotswap process and enforces the Gaussian moat crossing as a terminal anchor.

⊢.chosen_element: void register before any IMASM word exists
⊢.justification: The uninitialized state prior to loading either word into the fusion arena; corresponds to the empty register 00 and the holographic state precondition V = L(x) ∧ selfmodel(x) ∧ x ∈ V.

⊣.chosen_element: fusion arena closure with moat seal
⊣.justification: The terminal anchor that seals the hotswap cycle; the cyclic topology (𐑥) ensures the fused pair cannot exit without completing the figure-8 exchange and crossing the Gaussian moat.

≻.justification: Forward morphism driving two distinct IMASM words toward the fusion interface via the bridge commutator; the low-barrier kinetics (𐑘) allow free exploration of the fused configuration.

≺.justification: Contravariant morphism executing the fission half of the hotswap; the Z2-protected transition (𐑴) guarantees the reverse path is topologically distinct from the forward path, with exact Frobenius inversion μ∘δ=id.

⋈.chosen_element: state transfer conduit with bridge stitch
⋈.justification: Sequential composition that chains the lossless state transfer across the scale-collapse boundary; the three-unit stitch and high-fidelity geometry (𐑐) ensure near-certain firing.

⊙.justification: Each IMASM word carries its own identity (monad ⊙) into the fusion; self-reference anchors the holographic state on both arms at the critical threshold (ξ→∞, PHI_C).

∈.chosen_element: conjunctive partner bifurcation with bridge existence
∈.justification: The fusion mechanism requires exactly two specific words simultaneously; FSPLIT opens the T-arm for word A and F-arm for word B as the required conjunctive pair, with bridge existence ∃y∈x(|y|∼|x|).

∋.chosen_element: fused word rejoin with tri-ancestral reconnection
∋.justification: Reunites the two arms after the hotswap cycle completes; conflicting arms rejoin to B (both states held) because the critical-phase exchange preserves both identities in superposition, and the Frobenius test confirms tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object that closes.

⊤.chosen_element: word A affirmative deposit on T-arm
⊤.justification: Deposits constructive truth (T) on the T-arm: word A's state is affirmatively transferred across the fusion interface via the bridge commutator.

⊥.chosen_element: word B affirmative deposit on F-arm
⊥.justification: Deposits constructive falsity (F) on the F-arm: word B's state is affirmatively transferred as the complementary partner; the Frobenius polarity (≺=𐑹) makes this the exact inverse operation.

⊞.justification: At the critical threshold (⊙=⊙), both word states are held simultaneously (B-state) without resolution; the correlation length diverges (ξ→∞) and μ∘δ=id holds exactly (PHI_C).

⊡.chosen_element: hotswap event record with winding fixation
⊡.justification: Permanent append-only record of each completed fusion-fission cycle; the Z2 winding invariant (𐑴: ∮_γ A = nπ ∧ n ∈ ℤ₂) fixes the topological charge of each cycle irreversibly.
